Implemented the Node.js tool at [output/main.js](/workspace/output/main.js), with the parser/runtime split across [output/bst.js](/workspace/output/bst.js), [output/bib.js](/workspace/output/bib.js), and [output/engine.js](/workspace/output/engine.js). It accepts the requested flags, writes `.bbl` on success, writes structured error JSON on failure, and optionally writes the structured JSON log.

The implementation covers the stock BibTeX pipeline you described: `.bst` parsing and execution, `.bib` parsing with style-defined and month macros, citation extraction from `--cites` and `--aux`, crossref materialization, canonical-style execution, and 79-column wrapped `.bbl` output. Failure handling includes malformed `.bib` / `.bst`, unreadable inputs, missing flags, undefined functions at load time, and runtime stack underflow.

I smoke-tested it against `plain.bst`, `alpha.bst`, `unsrt.bst`, and `abbrv.bst`, plus targeted cases for unresolved macros, quoted undefined functions, crossrefs, wrapping, and fatal stack underflow. Direct comparison against a historical `bibtex` binary was not possible in this environment because no local `bibtex` executable was available.
